title: The Ted Heath package tour and warnings about Birmingham
summary: The package with Ted Heath, June Christie and Gary Morton was warned that Birmingham did not want white and black acts on one stage.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Gary Morton. It was Gary Morton, June Christie, Ted Heath, and Nat Cole, you know, on that segment of it. That was when the incident happened in Birmingham, Alabama. Do you remember? When they tried to kill him on the stage at Birmingham, Alabama?
I don't remember now. I must have known then, because ...

Yeah, because there were headlines in the paper. So, well, they didn't want acts mixed, you know, they didn't want white and black acts on the same stage in Birmingham, Alabama. But we were warned before we went there that they didn't want it and that there might be trouble. And so we went ahead anyway. And so Nat was getting ready to ...
Oh. It was the same package you had in England?
No, we didn't have that package in England; I think you misunderstood me.
I said the next time the exchange was Ted Heath came to the states, and that's when Stan Kenton went to Europe ...
And then we had the group with Ted Heath and June Christie and Gary Morton and Nat.
Then we went out with another ...
